subject: Day 27: end of week 4; plan the enrichment pipeline
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 27. End of week four. Feeding cadence is stable and the first social smile may already have appeared. Tomorrow opens the peak-crying weeks — a good moment to line up the enrichment and care pipeline before the harder evenings arrive.

Action items
- If the 1-month visit is still pending, confirm or schedule it today. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Read up on the peak-crying curve before the peak so the coming evenings feel expected, not alarming. AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- Lock daycare or nanny start dates; coordinate a 1-2 week overlap with paid leave if possible. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- Order pumping supplies if Anoushka will pump after returning to work; the double-electric pump is typically covered by insurance under the ACA.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Smoother, more symmetric arm and leg movements; first social smiles; evening fussiness starting to build toward the witching hour.
- [low concern] Cradle cap; a blocked tear duct without redness.
- [monitor] Persistent low mood or anxiety in Anoushka — the EPDS rescreen is one to two weeks out at the postpartum visit.
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting with weight loss, or fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Research a Bay Area parent-baby swim class and join a waitlist now; many SF programs start at three to six months and fill early. AAP HealthyChildren on swim lessons: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/safety-prevention/at-play/Pages/Swim-Lessons.aspx
- Lay him on a blanket on the grass in shade for a few minutes of new tactile and visual input; end before any sign of overstimulation. AAP HealthyChildren on infant senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Read aloud daily; start a rotation of three to five board books so the repetition builds rhythm and predictability. Reach Out and Read evidence base: https://reachoutandread.org/
- Tummy time 20 minutes a day, building toward the 30-minute week-six target. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: peak-crying curve begins.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit (if not yet done).
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines.
